title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC1RE_1RA1LD_0LC0LA_1RF1RD_---0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC1RE_1RA1LD_0LC0LA_1RF1RD_---0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is mostly two blocks: an alternating block (10)^x and a solid block 1^y. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) finds no halt in the first 1015 steps; the jump map in C finds no halt in the first 8.1·1029 steps, and the pass map in C none in the first 6.5·1032, and the closed pass map in C none in the first 2.0·1034.

What Lean proves. The whole frame map: 8 tape shapes, 78 cases, each proved for all sizes by a symbolic run (next_sound), and the cases where the map is undefined halt (none_halts). So the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from the frame the run reaches after 2 steps, reaches one of those cases (halts_iff). By native_decide the first 108 frames (about 4.5·1011 machine steps) do not. With whole sweeps taken as one jump (lean/Jump.lean), native_decide extends this to 1.5·1014 frames, and five halting rows are proved: a halt needs a zigzag to start exactly on one of them. lean/Pass.lean proves the whole pass from one zigzag start to the next as one affine map away from those rows, and extends the check to 3.9·1015 frames. lean/Close.lean closes the pass map: every pass near the boundary is one of 89 more affine cases or a halting row, so the machine halts iff the orbit of y(3, 0, 5) under one total map on three numbers lands on y(a, j, a/3 + 2) or Y(a, j, a/3 + 3) with a ≡ 1 mod 3 (halts_iff_row). Whether it ever does is open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,302 cells have been visited and 3,792 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.321). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.347).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) runs 1015 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: Two blocks trading length
claims.text: At the moments the head reaches a new cell between steps 9.79·10<sup>7</sup> and 9.94·10<sup>7</sup>, the tape is an alternating block and a solid block plus a few cells, with lengths (806, 336), (672, 604), (540, 874), (722, 513).

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state F was entered 83,257 times, always reading a 1 (F0 halts).

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the machine on a grid
claims.text: For each of the 8 frames and every canonical choice of sizes below 16, the machine reaches exactly the frame, sizes and step count the fitted map predicts (30,736 frames, py/framemap.py verify 16). The map is now proved in Lean; this check is how it was found.

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the run
claims.text: Run from blank tape next to the machine, the fitted map predicts the whole tape at each of the 48,691 frames in the first 5·106 steps (py/framemap.py real 5000000).

claims.title: The whole frame map
claims.text: next in lean/Phases.lean sends each of the 8 frames to the next one the machine reaches, in 78 cases; next_sound proves every case for all parameters, each from a symbolic run in lean/Pieces.lean (generated by py/pieces.py) glued by tape_eq. Where next is undefined (.z 1 1 1, .w l 0 1, .w l 1 0, .W l 0 1, .W l 1 0) the machine halts (none_halts).

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map reaches an undefined case
claims.text: init_start: the run from blank tape reaches Ph.z 0 0 2 after 2 steps. halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from there is a frame where next is none.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames
claims.text: no_halt_phases, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates are defined. By the step counts of the fitted map (py/framemap.py run 100000000) that is about 4.5·1011 machine steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.58·10<sup>22</sup> steps (accelerated run, blocks of 2)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/c/rleaccel.cpp (blocks of 2 cells, runs of a block crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths above the minimums it needs; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 1,404,600,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt, in 600 seconds. That is more than 3.58·1022 machine steps. It found no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: Whole sweeps and zigzags in closed form
claims.text: w_sweep, u_sweep, y_zigzag and their bracket twins: k repetitions of one case of next (two for a zigzag round) for all sizes, e.g. y(a + 3k, j, r + 1 + k) reaches y(a, j + 2k, r + 1) in 2k frames. jump takes each whole sweep or zigzag at once and jump_sound proves every jump is that many frames of next.

claims.title: Five halting rows
claims.text: halt_y: from y(3k+1, 2m, k+2) the map reaches a frame where it is undefined (k zigzag rounds, three frames, a sweep to w(., 0, 1)); likewise halt_Y for Y(3k+1, 2m, k+3), and halt_y0, halt_y2, halt_Y0 for three rows with an odd alternating block.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.5·10<sup>14</sup> frames
claims.text: jumps_frames, by native_decide: 108 jumps from Ph.z 0 0 2 are defined and cover 146,530,202,670,678 frames of next; no_halt_frames: none of them is a halting frame (8.1·1020 machine steps by the step counts of the cases).

claims.title: No halt in the first 8.1·10<sup>29</sup> steps (the jump map)
claims.text: c/frun.c iterates the jump map with 64-bit sizes and 128-bit step counts (the 78 cases generated from the Lean files by py/gen_c.py; every jump checked case by case by frun check and against the Lean cases by py/check_frun.py): 1.0·1011 jumps, 1.5·1020 frames, 8.1·1029 machine steps, no halt.

claims.title: The pass map: one zigzag start to the next
claims.text: Away from the line where both blocks run out together (within 6 of r = ⌊a/3⌋), the run from one zigzag start to the next is one affine map: a drain t(a, j, r) → t(a − 3r + 1, 0, 4r + 2j + 2) or a growth t(a, j, r) → t'(4q + 2j + c, 0, r − q − d) with a = 3q + e and (t', c, d) from a table of 11 rows. 13 theorems, each a chain of the jump lemmas with its exact frame count; pass_sound: a pass is that many frames of the frame map.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.9·10<sup>15</sup> frames
claims.text: passes_frames, by native_decide: 108 passes from Ph.z 0 0 2 are defined and cover 3,893,676,335,181,895 frames of next; no_halt_passes: none of them is a halting frame (1.1·1023 machine steps by the step counts of the cases).

claims.title: No halt in the first 6.5·10<sup>32</sup> steps (the pass map)
claims.text: c/prun.c iterates the pass map (the 13 cases of lean/Pass.lean, jumps near the boundary) with 64-bit sizes and 128-bit counts; checked pass by pass against frun on the first 2·1010 passes (prun check): 1.8·1011 passes, 1.3·1022 frames, 6.5·1032 machine steps, no halt.

claims.title: The closed pass map
claims.text: Every pass from a zigzag start within 6 of the boundary is one of 89 affine cases or one of the five halting rows, for all sizes; with the 13 cases of lean/Pass.lean the pass map cpass is total on zigzag starts (cpass_total), sound (cpass_go, cpass_halt), keeps j even (cpass_even) and halts exactly on the two rows with j even (cpass_halt_iff).

claims.title: Halting is landing on one of two lines
claims.text: halts_iff_row: the machine halts from blank tape iff the orbit of y(3, 0, 5) under the closed pass map reaches y(a, j, r) with a ≡ 1 (mod 3), r = ⌊a/3⌋ + 2 or Y(a, j, r) with a ≡ 1 (mod 3), r = ⌊a/3⌋ + 3.

claims.title: No row in the first 100,000,000 closed passes
claims.text: orb_frames, by native_decide: the orbit is defined for 100,000,000 passes (3,893,689,985,794,413 frames); no_row: none of them is on a row.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.0·10<sup>34</sup> steps (the closed map, growth runs as one step)
claims.text: c/crun.c takes whole growth runs by residue tables mod 3k, checked step by step against the pass-by-pass map on 2·1010 passes: 570,000,000,003 passes, 1.3·1023 frames, 2.0·1034 machine steps, no halt.

claims.title: A halt is expected, around 10<sup>14</sup> passes
claims.text: A pass is the map x → 4x/3 or 4x − 3 on x = a/(a + j + r), and a halt needs x to land on 3/4 to the cell. Near the boundary the run matches a uniform spread at the scale of one cell (285 starts within 16 of it in 10<sup>11</sup> passes, 290 expected), which gives a hazard of about 0.22 hits per unit of Σ1/N, N growing by about 2 a pass (random orbits of the map: 0.08 to 0.47). So the expected number of hits grows like ln of the pass count, 0.24 per factor 10; about 2 were expected from pass 1,000 to 10<sup>11</sup> and none came (chance about 14%). Median halt if this holds: about 10<sup>14</sup> passes, 10<sup>41</sup> steps, weeks of one core. (The earlier ln ln J estimate, median 10<sup>53</sup> steps, took epochs to lengthen; they do not.)

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape is an alternating block and a solid block whose lengths trade back and forth; each pass rewrites one block into the other.

facts.text: No halt in 5.7·1011 passes of the closed pass map (c/crun.c, growth runs as one step).
It halts iff the orbit of the closed pass map lands on one of two lines (lean/Close.lean).
No halt in 1.8·1011 passes of the pass map (c/prun.c), each from one zigzag start to the next.
No halt in the first 108 passes, checked in Lean by native_decide (no_halt_passes).
Zigzag starts that halt, e.g. y(3k+1, 2m, k+2); the run must land exactly on one to halt.
It halts if and only if the frame map, iterated from the first frame, reaches a frame where it is undefined.
No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells).
An alternating and a solid block trade length.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 4,302 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell. With a for 10, around step 9.8·107:

• step 97,915,409: D>0 a^2 1 a^802 1^338 (left end)
  • step 97,921,865: A>0^2 a^806 1^336 (left end)
  • step 98,376,215: 1^2 a 1^604 a^672 C>0 (right end)
  • step 98,837,298: A>0^2 a^540 1^874 (left end)
  • step 99,362,025: C>0^2 a^722 1^513 (left end)

The tape is two long blocks, one alternating and one solid, and at successive moments their lengths trade: 806 copies of 10 and 336 ones, then 604 ones and 672 copies of 10, then 540 and 874, then 722 and 513. Rewriting a block of length x costs about x passes of length x, so the width grows like the cube root of the step count. The shape is the one of the three machines 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_…_1RF0LD_---0RE, where one block doubles at the other's expense. The exact rules are the frame map below; the epochs they make, a growth phase where one block grows by 4/3 a pass and a drain phase where the other grows by 4, are in Whole sweeps as one jump.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is F reading a 0. F is entered only from E reading a 0 (1RF), so a halt needs E>0 0. In the first 108 steps F was entered 83,257 times, every time on a 1, and 82,807 of those times at least 7 cells from the left end.
At the level of the frame map, a halt needs a zigzag to start exactly on one of five rows; see The halting rows and the close calls. Whether the run ever lands on one is open.

sections.heading: The frame map in Lean
html: The frames (blank tape outside; X is the head in state X on the next cell; u^v is v copies of u, so 11^L is 2L ones; a frame counts only at a moment where the head turns round):

• z: 1^L 10^j C 1^R
  • y: 1^L A 10 10^j 1^R
  • w: 1^L C 00 10^j 1^R
  • u: 1^L 10^j 1 A 00 1^R
  • Z: 1110 1^L 10^j C 1^R
  • Y: 1110 1^L A 10 10^j 1^R
  • W: 1110 1^L C 00 10^j 1^R
  • U: 1110 1^L 10^j 1 A 00 1^R
The map next (Lean names; each variable a natural number):

The map was found by fitting the machine's runs (py/framemap.py) and collapsing the fit into cases (py/pieces.py); Lean then checks every case for all sizes. It is undefined only at .z 1 1 1, .w l 0 1, .w l 1 0, .W l 0 1, .W l 1 0, and those halt. So the open question is exactly whether the orbit of Ph.z 0 0 2 reaches one of them; the first 108 frames do not.

sections.heading: Exact tapes, exact step counts
html:
The same frame map written the way the bbchallenge wiki writes Antihydra's: name the tapes exactly, then list the rules, each with the exact number of machine steps it takes. The Lean map works frame by frame, so the families are its eight frames (the head is on the cell after >; Z, Y, W, U are z, y, w, u with a bracket 1110 at the left end):

z(l, j, r) := 0∞ 1l (10)j C> 1r 0∞
y(l, j, r) := 0∞ 1l A> 10 (10)j 1r 0∞
w(l, j, r) := 0∞ 1l C> 00 (10)j 1r 0∞
u(l, j, r) := 0∞ 1l (10)j 1 A> 00 1r 0∞
Z(l, j, r) := 0∞ 1110 1l (10)j C> 1r 0∞, and Y, W, U in the same way.

Most of the time the head zigzags: a zig and a zag turn three 1s of the left block and one of the right block into two more 10 pairs. When the zigzag reaches the left end, a w sweep turns the pairs back into 1s on the left (two pairs into four 1s per round); when it reaches the right end, a u sweep turns them into 1s on the right (one pair into two 1s per round).

Every row except the k-round rows is one case of next, or a few cases glued together (the zig is .z (l + 2) 0 (r + 1) and .z (l + 2) (j + 1) (r + 1)), and each is a theorem: next_sound in lean/Phases.lean for the moves, none_halts for the halts, init_start for the start. The step count of each case is in Lean too: it is the step number in the statement of the case's piece theorem in lean/Pieces.lean (the zig for j ≥ 1 is pc_z13b, steps (2 * j + 4)), although next_sound itself only says that some number of steps exists. A halting row counts the steps of its piece up to F on a 0, plus the halting step. The k-round rows are sums of k such cases and are not stated in Lean. With halts_iff, the machine halts iff these rules, started at z(0, 0, 2), reach a halt row.

The table leaves out the remaining cases of next (78 in all; the table uses 29): the small values of l, j and r listed in the frame map section above, with step counts from 2 to 26, or 2j + 8, 6j + 12 and 6j + 18. In the first 107 steps from blank tape they are used 14 times out of 77,045 moves. python3 py/rules.py reads the cases and their step counts from the two Lean files and checks them against direct simulation: all 78 cases on 5,832 frames (every variable below 9), every row of the table with its bracket variants on 25,957 instances (k up to 6), and every frame of the first 107 steps from blank tape, where the tapes agree and the step counts add up.

For example u(11, 0, 3) = 112 A> 00 13: back from u (4 steps) to y(10, 0, 5), a zag (3) to z(9, 2, 4), three zigzag rounds (63) to z(0, 8, 1), to w (18) at w(0, 8, 1), a w sweep of four rounds (24) to w(16, 0, 1), and the halt (5): 117 steps in all, which is what direct simulation gives.

sections.heading: Whole sweeps as one jump
html: Almost every frame of the map repeats one of a few cases, and the repeats add up in closed form, proved for all sizes in lean/Jump.lean:

w(l, j + 2k, r + 1)      k frames, 6k steps              w(l + 4k, j, r + 1)     w_sweep (also W)
u(l, j + k, r)           k frames, 4k steps              u(l, j, r + 2k)         u_sweep (also U)
y(a + 3k, j, r + 1 + k)  2k frames, k(4j+9) + 4k(k-1)    y(a, j + 2k, r + 1)     y_zigzag (also Y)

A jump takes a whole sweep or zigzag at once and is one case of the map otherwise (jump, jump_sound). The run from blank tape is then about 108 jumps per 1.5·1014 frames, and the shape of the run becomes visible. Write the tape as a solid block 1^l (blue below), an alternating block (10)^j (purple) and a solid block 1^r (amber). An epoch has two phases:

• Growth. A zigzag turns the left block into alternating cells (each round eats 3 of the left block and 1 of the right block), and a w sweep turns them back into a left block 4/3 as long. The left block grows by 4/3 a pass and the right block pays a third of it, until the right block runs out in the middle of a zigzag.
  • Drain. A u sweep moves the alternating block into the right block, and the zigzags now stop when the right block runs out, each pass multiplying it by about 4 and eating three times as much of the left block, until the left block is gone and a new epoch starts.

Inside a phase the ratios are fixed. What is chaotic is where the phases end: the remainders at the crossovers. The tape grows by a few cells a pass, so the sizes grow about linearly in the number of jumps and the step count like its cube.

sections.heading: The halting rows and the close calls
html: A zigzag stops when the left block is below 3 or the right block is down to 1. When both run out together, three more frames and a sweep decide, and five rows end in a frame where the map is undefined (halt_y, halt_Y, halt_y0, halt_y2, halt_Y0 in lean/Jump.lean):

zigzag startthen
y(3k+1, 2m, k+2)k rounds to y(1, ., 2), z(0, ., 1), w(0, even, 1), a sweep to w(., 0, 1): halt
Y(3k+1, 2m, k+3)k rounds to Y(1, ., 3), z(2, ., 2), y(0, odd, 2), z(0, ., 1), w(0, even, 1), a sweep: halt
y(3k, 2m+1, k+2), y(3k+2, 2m+1, k+2), Y(3k, 2m+1, k+2)the same with an odd alternating block

From every frame with all three numbers below 60, every halt within 400 jumps comes before the first zigzag or right after a zigzag start in one of these rows (frun rows 60; not proved for all frames). In the run from blank tape every zigzag start so far has an even alternating block, so only the first two rows can be met: the machine halts if a crossover lands on y(a, 2m, R) with a = 3R − 5 or Y(a, 2m, R) with a = 3R − 8. Call d the distance to the row (d = R − ⌊a/3⌋ − 2, or −3 for Y, at starts with a ≡ 1 mod 3).

The jump map in C (c/frun.c) ran 1.0·1011 jumps, 1.5·1020 frames, 8.1·1029 machine steps, without a halt (the earlier accelerated run stopped at 3.58·1022). Every zigzag start within 16 of a halting row (blue: y, purple: Y; hover for the frame):

Heuristic. An earlier version of this page took an epoch to last about log J jumps and got an expected number of hits growing like ln ln J. An epoch lasts a bounded number of passes on average (a pass ends the growth with chance about 1/4), so the count grows like ln J; the section on passes below measures the rate.

sections.heading: Passes: the whole run as a map of one number
html: A pass runs from one zigzag start to the next: a zigzag, a few single frames and a sweep. Away from the line where both blocks run out together it is one affine map, proved for all sizes in lean/Pass.lean (13 theorems, each a chain of the jump lemmas, with its exact frame count). Write the zigzag start t(a, j, r) with t = y or Y and a = 3q + e:

drain   r ≤ q − 1:  t(a, j, r)  →  t(a − 3r + 1, 0, 4r + 2j + 2)       drain_y, drain_Y
growth  r ≥ q + 7:  t(a, j, r)  →  t'(4q + 2j + c, 0, r − q − d)       grow_*

        t e  j even: t' c d   j odd: t' c d
        y 0          y  2 1          y  5 4
        y 1          y  7 4          y  4 1
        y 2          Y  2 1          Y  5 4
        Y 0          y  5 1          y  8 4
        Y 1          y 11 5          y  8 2
        Y 2          y(5, j + 2q + 2, r − q − 1)  (a short zigzag follows)

Only within 6 of the line r = q does the run go back to jumps, and that is where all five halting rows lie (d = 0 means r − q = 2 for y and 3 for Y). In the run from blank tape that happens about once in 108 passes. pass is the 13 cases where they apply and a jump elsewhere; pass_sound proves each pass is that many frames of the frame map, and native_decide runs 108 passes (passes_frames): no halt in the first 3.9·1015 frames (no_halt_passes, 1.1·1023 machine steps), against 1.5·1014 by 108 jumps.

One number. In both cases the total N = a + j + r (j is 0 at almost every start) changes by a few cells only, so the state is essentially the fraction x = a/N, and a pass is the map x → 4x/3 (growth, x < 3/4) or x → 4x − 3 (drain): two full branches of slopes 4/3 and 4, whose invariant density is uniform. The epochs of the section above are runs of the first branch ended by one step of the second. A halt needs x to land exactly on the branch point 3/4, to the cell. The panel runs the pass map from blank tape (BigInt; the same passes as c/prun.c on the first 300,000, py/pass_panel_test.js) and draws the last 40 values of x:

The run. c/prun.c iterates the pass map with 64-bit sizes and 128-bit step counts, 5.7 times as fast as the jump map, and agrees with frun pass by pass on the first 2·1010 passes (prun check) and on the frame, frame count and step count after 109 jumps. It ran 1.8·1011 passes, 1.3·1022 frames, 6.5·1032 machine steps, without a halt:

How likely is a halt. If x were spread uniformly at the scale of one cell, a pass would land on a given row with chance about 1/(4N), and N grows by about 2 a pass, so the expected number of hits grows like the logarithm of the pass count (not like ln ln J: an epoch lasts a bounded number of passes on average). The run follows this model: the first 1011 passes have 285 zigzag starts within 16 of the boundary, 0.98 of the uniform count, and 84 within 16 of a row, 0.87 of it (py/near.py; N = a + j + r). That gives a halting hazard of 0.22 per unit of Σ1/N. Random orbits of the same map (prun rate, 4,307 halts, every one right after a start with d = 0) give between 0.08 and 0.47 depending on the size, as orbits of the map merge and are far from independent. For the run from blank tape Σ1/N is 9.1 from pass 1,000 to 1011, so about 2.0 hits were expected there (chance of none 14%); each further factor 10 of passes adds about 0.24. If that holds the machine halts with probability 1, with a median around 1014 passes and 1041 steps, which the pass map reaches in about 21 days of one core (the earlier estimate was 1053 steps).

sections.heading: The closed pass map
html: The 13 cases of the section above leave out the passes within 6 of the line r = q. lean/Close.lean closes the map: for each tag (y or Y), each e = a mod 3, each parity of j and each δ = r − q from 0 to 6 the pass is again one chain of zigzags, sweeps and single frames, the same for all sizes (one exception splits off the sizes q = 1). That is 89 more theorems, generated by py/gen_close.py from the jumps of c/prun.c and checked by Lean for all q and j. Exactly five classes do not reach a next zigzag start: they are the five halting rows.

So cpass, the pass map with these cases, is defined on every zigzag start and gives either the next zigzag start with its frame count or a halt (cpass_total, cpass_go, cpass_halt). Every case maps an even alternating block to an even one (cpass_even), and the run from blank tape reaches its first zigzag start y(3, 0, 5) after 6 frames, so the three rows with odd j can never be met. Lean then proves the reduction:

halts_iff_row. The machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of y(3, 0, 5) under the closed pass map reaches y(a, j, r) with a ≡ 1 (mod 3) and r = ⌊a/3⌋ + 2, or Y(a, j, r) with a ≡ 1 (mod 3) and r = ⌊a/3⌋ + 3.

This replaces the frame map, the jumps and the near-boundary fallback with one total map on three numbers and a target set of two lines. orb_frames runs 100,000,000 closed passes by native_decide (ending at Y(131,674,078, 0, 76,026,925), 3,893,689,985,794,413 frames after the first zigzag start) and no_row follows: none of them is on a row.

Growth runs in one step. A growth pass sends a = 3q + e to 4q + c with c fixed by the tag and e, so k growth passes in a row depend only on a mod 3k: with a = 3kQ + ρ the end state, the frames and the steps are polynomials in Q (degrees 1, 1 and 2), and the k passes are all growth passes iff r is at least a linear function of Q (the margin r − q − 7 shrinks every pass, so the last one decides). c/crun.c builds these tables for k ≤ 7 at start-up from the single-pass formulas, by exact interpolation checked on further points and at the edge of the condition, and takes each growth run with the deepest table that applies; a drain is one step and the rare near passes go by jumps. It agrees with the pass-by-pass iteration (state, frames and steps) at every one of the 8.6·109 table steps of the first 2·1010 passes (crun check), and runs about 8.5·107 passes a second, 2.6 times prun on the same core. A halt can only come from a near pass, which is never inside a table, and every start with |d| ≤ 3 is a drain or a near pass, so the close calls below are complete.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.321). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.347).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,302 cells (2,289 left of the start, 1,181 right), with a density of 1s of 0.881.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: doubling between an alternating and a solid block
summary: Its tape is an alternating block and a solid block whose lengths trade back and forth; each pass rewrites one block into the other. Pass map: no halt in 6.45e32 steps. Closed pass map: no halt in 2.05e34 steps.
